exempt.reason: §7 names what the decision leaves undecided (the Project header label); it makes no behaviour to test

specs.description: --lang js writes the whole JavaScript counter layout.
specs.given: a fresh empty directory and Node 22 or later
specs.when: hexa init <dir> --name my-app --scaffold --lang js --no-claude-md runs
specs.then: The directory holds exactly package.json, src/core/domain/count.js, src/core/ports/counter-store.js, src/core/usecases/increment.js, src/adapters/secondary/in-memory-counter-store.js, src/composition-root.js and src/counter.test.js, beside hexa's own files.

specs.description: package.json declares the project, a version, ES modules, the minimum Node and the test script.
specs.given: a fresh empty directory and Node 22 or later
specs.when: the JavaScript scaffold is written for a project named my-app
specs.then: package.json is JSON naming my-app, version 0.1.0, type module, engines.node >=22 and a scripts.test that runs node --test.

specs.description: The port re-exports the domain's Count and documents the store, and the test exercises the composition root.
specs.given: a fresh empty directory and Node 22 or later
specs.when: the JavaScript scaffold is written
specs.then: src/core/ports/counter-store.js exports Count from the domain and carries a JSDoc typedef for CounterStore with load and save, and src/counter.test.js imports the composition root and calls it.

specs.description: The in-memory adapter does not import the domain or the use cases.
specs.given: a fresh empty directory and Node 22 or later
specs.when: the JavaScript scaffold is written
specs.then: src/adapters/secondary/in-memory-counter-store.js imports only src/core/ports/counter-store.js.

specs.description: No placeholder or template suffix survives in the JavaScript output.
specs.given: a fresh empty directory and Node 22 or later
specs.when: the JavaScript scaffold is written for a project named my-app
specs.then: No written file contains {{ or }}, none is named *.tmpl, and package.json carries the name my-app.

specs.description: The JavaScript gate is node --test and passes on a fresh scaffold.
specs.given: a fresh empty directory and Node 22 or later
specs.when: node --test runs in the scaffolded project
specs.then: It exits 0 and reports 4 tests passed and 0 failed.

specs.description: SCAFFOLD_LANGS names js with its gate command.
specs.given: the hexa binary
specs.when: the scaffold languages are read
specs.then: js is listed and its gate command is node --test.

specs.description: The JavaScript gate needs no install step and no network.
specs.given: a fresh empty directory and Node 22 or later
specs.when: the scaffold is written and node --test runs with no network and no node_modules
specs.then: The tests pass; package.json has no dependencies and no devDependencies and no node_modules directory was needed.

specs.description: A failing or empty node --test run does not count as a passing gate.
specs.given: a scaffolded JavaScript project with one assertion changed to fail, and another with no test file
specs.when: the gate is judged by hexa's evidence reader
specs.then: The failing run is a failure and the run with no test is not a pass.

specs.description: Every import is a relative path with its .js extension that names a scaffolded file.
specs.given: a fresh empty directory and Node 22 or later
specs.when: the JavaScript scaffold is written
specs.then: Each import specifier in a written .js file either starts with ./ or ../ and ends in .js and resolves to a scaffolded file, or is a node: built-in.

specs.description: No import names a package from a registry.
specs.given: a fresh empty directory and Node 22 or later
specs.when: the JavaScript scaffold is written
specs.then: No import specifier in a written file is a bare package name; the only non-relative ones begin with node:.

specs.description: The JavaScript ignore lines include node_modules/.
specs.given: the gitignore lines for js
specs.when: they are read
specs.then: node_modules/ is among them.

specs.description: JavaScript's ignore lines are JavaScript's only.
specs.given: the gitignore lines for js
specs.when: they are read
specs.then: They do not include dist/, target/, __pycache__/ or .venv/.

specs.description: A merged JavaScript .gitignore holds each JavaScript line exactly once.
specs.given: any existing .gitignore text
specs.when: the js lines are merged into it twice
specs.then: Each js line appears exactly once, and the existing lines are kept.

specs.description: hexa analyze grades the fresh JavaScript scaffold A+ with full coverage.
specs.given: a fresh empty directory and Node 22 or later
specs.when: the scaffold is written and hexa analyze --json runs on it
specs.then: The grade is A+, the score is 100, there are no violations, cycles or dead exports, and every graded file is in a layer.

specs.description: The JavaScript scaffold satisfies the domain policy it ships.
specs.given: a fresh empty directory and Node 22 or later
specs.when: the scaffold is written and its shipped ADR rules are checked
specs.then: The domain file imports nothing from outside the domain and no policy violation is reported.

specs.description: No JavaScript scaffold file is left unclassified or in the wrong layer.
specs.given: a fresh empty directory and Node 22 or later
specs.when: the scaffold is written and hexa analyze --json runs
specs.then: Each source file is in the layer its folder names, the composition root is in the composition-root layer and the unclassified list is empty.

specs.description: A fresh JavaScript scaffold needs no edit before its gate passes.
specs.given: a fresh empty directory and Node 22 or later
specs.when: the scaffold is written and node --test runs at once
specs.then: The gate passes with no change to any file.

specs.description: The JavaScript scaffold is deterministic.
specs.given: two empty directories
specs.when: the scaffold is written into each with one project name
specs.then: Both hold the same files with the same bytes.

specs.description: --lang still defaults to rust.
specs.given: a fresh empty directory
specs.when: hexa init --scaffold runs with no --lang
specs.then: A Rust project is written, not a JavaScript one.

specs.description: An unknown --lang is refused and names js among the known ones.
specs.given: a fresh empty directory
specs.when: hexa init --scaffold --lang cobol runs
specs.then: It fails, writes nothing, and its message lists js among the languages it knows.

specs.description: The Rust, Go, TypeScript and Python scaffolds are byte-for-byte unchanged.
specs.given: each of those four languages
specs.when: the scaffold is written for a project named my-app
specs.then: The files and their bytes are those the scaffold wrote before this decision.

specs.description: A JavaScript scaffold never overwrites an existing file.
specs.given: a directory that already holds a package.json with its own content
specs.when: hexa init --scaffold --lang js runs there
specs.then: The existing package.json is unchanged and the other scaffold files are still written.
